name: pwm_controller
description: Parameterized PWM controller with synchronous enable-controlled counter, period-based wrap/reset, duty-cycle comparison, and synchronous active-low reset to zero.

fixed_assumptions: Single-clock synchronous design sampled on rising edge of clk.
All state elements reset to 0 when reset_n is low.

period is treated as an inclusive terminal count value; when counter_value equals period and enable is high on a clock edge, the counter wraps to 0 on that edge before the next-cycle outputs are observed.
If period is 0, the counter remains at 0 while enable is high.
pwm_out is a combinational function of the registered counter_value and duty_cycle.
duty_cycle and period are sampled as inputs and may change cycle to cycle; no shadow registers are implied.

feature_contracts.description: Verify synchronous active-low reset clears the counter and produces a comparison-based PWM output from the cleared count.
Verify that with reset deasserted and enable low, the counter holds its previous value while pwm_out continues to reflect the current counter and duty-cycle comparison.
Verify that the counter increments by one on a clock edge when enable is high and reset is deasserted.
Verify that the counter wraps to zero when the registered count reaches period and enable remains high.
Verify pwm_out is low when the registered counter_value is not less than duty_cycle.
Verify that a zero period causes the counter to remain at zero while enable is high.

functionality: Implements a programmable pulse-width modulator. The internal 8-bit counter increments by one on each rising clock edge when enable is asserted. The counter wraps to zero when its registered value reaches the programmed period value, otherwise it continues incrementing. The PWM output is asserted when the registered counter_value is strictly less than duty_cycle, providing a pulse width proportional to duty_cycle within each period. Reset forces the counter and all registered state to zero, and pwm_out is then determined by the comparison of the reset-cleared counter_value against duty_cycle.
responsibilities: Provide a synthesizable PWM timing source using only the declared ports.
Maintain an observable 8-bit counter_value output that reflects the current registered count.
Generate a duty-cycle-dependent pwm_out with deterministic comparison against the registered counter.
Honor synchronous reset and enable semantics exactly as specified.
Avoid any hidden state, memory, or extra handshakes beyond the declared interface.
reset_behavior: When reset_n is low, the design synchronously clears the internal counter register to 8'h00. The counter_value output reflects this cleared state. pwm_out is a combinational decode of counter_value < duty_cycle, so after reset it is 1 whenever duty_cycle is nonzero and 0 when duty_cycle is 0.
behavior_rules: On each rising edge of clk, if reset_n is low, set counter_value to 8'h00.
On each rising edge of clk, if reset_n is high and enable is low, hold counter_value constant.
On each rising edge of clk, if reset_n is high and enable is high and counter_value equals period, load counter_value with 8'h00.
On each rising edge of clk, if reset_n is high and enable is high and counter_value is less than period, increment counter_value by 8'h01.
pwm_out shall be 1 when counter_value < duty_cycle and 0 otherwise.
counter_value is the registered count; pwm_out is a combinational decode of the registered count and duty_cycle.
The design shall be free of latches and use only synthesizable SystemVerilog constructs.
Inputs are unsigned 8-bit values; comparison and wrap decisions use unsigned arithmetic semantics.
